feed.title: Business News - Markets reports and financial news from Sky

articles.title: Microsoft offers 'buyouts' to 60,000 staff including UK workers
articles.summary: Microsoft is offering voluntary severance packages to 60,000 of its staff - more than a quarter of its workforce - including some in the UK.

articles.title: Curzon Cinemas-owner Fortress screen-tests potential bidders
articles.summary: The owner of Curzon Cinemas is exploring a sale of the business following a number of unsolicited bid approaches.

articles.title: Lions sponsor Howden lines up ex-Goldman partner for board amid fundraising
articles.summary: The insurance broker Howden Group is lining up a former Goldman Sachs partner to strengthen boardroom governance amid talks with investors about a multibillion-pound fundraising.

articles.title: Anthropic reveals plans for blockbuster IPO
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence giant Anthropic, the company behind the popular Claude chatbot, has filed papers to sell shares to the public for the first time.

articles.title: Struggling London-listed media group Future rebuffs interest in The Week
articles.summary: The struggling London-listed company which owns Go Compare, the price comparison platform, has rebuffed indicative bid interest in The Week, the current affairs magazine.

articles.title: PM open to 'honest discussion' about return to EU free movement
articles.summary: Andy Burnham says that an "honest discussion" is needed about readopting the EU's free movement rules.

articles.title: Former Goldman Sachs chief leaves Britain amid tax hike fears
articles.summary: A former Goldman Sachs chief who sits on the board of Revolut, Europe's most valuable private technology company, has become the latest prominent financier to leave the country amid concerns about Britain’s rising tax burden.

articles.title: Volvo Cars in share price crash as 2,500 job cuts follow sales slump
articles.summary: Volvo Cars has revealed a further 2,500 job cuts amid a slump in sales that has seen its share price crash to record lows.

articles.title: The £1,000 mistake people are making with new iPhone purchase
articles.summary: Apple's new iPhone Duo is the company's first foldable device - but at £1,999, it's not cheap.

articles.title: Winter energy supply secure but possible 'tight days' for electricity - grid operators
articles.summary: Britain's energy supplies are secure for winter, national grid operators have said, despite expected higher gas demand at peak times and possible "tight days" for electricity.
